name: The Nation cryptic crossword No 3483
preamble: Puzzled? No more cross words! Read Kosman and Picciotto on “Solving The Nation’s Cryptic Puzzles.” Or watch this video.

clue.text: God rested by vessel

blocks.note: rested on a seat, past tense
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: A deity takes a break beside a jar or pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is the Roman deity of agriculture and time, an example of a god.

clue.text: Engineer sees a cap in maritime artwork

indicators.note: to engineer is to construct or rearrange, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A ship's engineer spots a cap in a painting of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting or picture of the sea, a marine work of art.

clue.text: Atrium is befouled with dessert

indicators.note: something befouled is messed up, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A hotel lobby gets dirtied with spilled pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian layered sweet of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, a pudding course.

clue.text: Lift handle with delight

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting a word turns it upside down, reading bottom to top

blocks.note: a lever is a handle you pull or push

explanation.surface: Raising a handle brings joy.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to take great pleasure or enjoyment, a verb matching delight.

clue.text: Something you might eat at the shore: gruesome, macabre bit of turtle

definitions.text: Something you might eat at the shore

indicators.note: something gruesome has been mangled, so the neighbouring word's letters are rearranged
a bit of a word is just a small part of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written, to be mixed
the first letter of turtle

explanation.surface: A beach snack described as a grisly chunk of a sea turtle.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabmeat is seafood often eaten at the seaside, so it fits as a shore-side meal.

clue.text: What a ghoul does outside a hospital area: start to taunt poet and novelist

indicators.note: one phrase goes outside the other, surrounding it
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a ghoul in folklore plunders burial sites
the emergency room
the first letter of taunt

explanation.surface: A ghoul lurks by an emergency ward to taunt a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The insert goes between the two words of the grave-robbing phrase, not around it as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Graves was the English author of the poems and the novel I, Claudius.

clue.text: Snack and case of beer uplifted Minnelli fan

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer shell, its first and last letters
in a down entry, uplifted means written upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: the outside letters of beer
Liza Minnelli, the singer and actress
a nut is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A snack and a crate of beer cheer up a Liza Minnelli devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazil nut is a large edible seed eaten as a nibble, an example of a snack.

clue.text: Belied treatment as safe, in a way

indicators.note: giving the word a treatment processes it into a new arrangement

blocks.note: letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A medical treatment was misrepresented as being safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' flags that edible is one kind of safe: safe to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food can be eaten without harm, which is one particular sense of safe.

clue.text: Guide to having great sex with many screaming fits?

definitions.text: Guide to having great sex with many screaming fits?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sex manual
setter's reading: the fits are cries of pleasure, and the word recalls tantrums

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a playful definition: 'screaming fits' sounds like tantrums, which the answer nearly spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantra is the Asian spiritual tradition popularly linked in the West with prolonged sexual practice.

clue.text: Appear in a stream, when moving from last to first place

indicators.text: when moving from last to first place
indicators.note: the final letter of the stream word travels to the front of it

blocks.note: taken as written
a river is a large stream

explanation.surface: Something turns up in a brook after shifting from the back of a race to the front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving from last to first place' sounds like a racing comeback, but it moves the stream word's final letter to its front.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive is to show up or make an appearance somewhere, a near synonym of appear.

clue.text: A piece of underwear is back on, with evidence of being worn

indicators.note: going back means the little word just before it is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
a bra is an item of lingerie
taken as written, then turned round
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worn-out bra is put on again, showing signs of heavy use.
explanation.definitionFit: An abrasion is a scrape or wearing away of a surface, the mark left by friction.

clue.text: Moans from dudes in Louisiana station with second delay

indicators.note: s is short for second, and delaying it sends that letter from the front to the end
one item placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the US state abbreviation
dudes are guys
taken as written, with its first letter then moved

explanation.surface: Men at a Louisiana railway station grumble when their train is late.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamentations are expressions of grief or complaint, plural nouns like moans.

clue.text: Rocker, say, clutching tattered lamé fabric

indicators.note: tattered cloth is torn apart, so the word next to it is rearranged
to clutch something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: a rocker is one kind of seat, hence 'say'
the shiny fabric's letters reordered

explanation.surface: A rock musician holding onto a ragged piece of glittery lamé cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocker' suggests a musician, but it is a rocking chair; the mixed letters sit after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Camel hair is a soft woollen cloth woven from the animal's coat, used for coats.

clue.text: Bette loses head for layabout

indicators.note: losing one's head means the opening letter is chopped off

blocks.note: Bette Midler, the singer and actress

explanation.surface: The singer Bette is fired and replaced by a lazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who does no work, the same as a lazy loafer.

clue.text: Motor, knockin', contains pebble by error

indicators.note: one thing containing another holds it inside, so the stone word sits within

blocks.note: an engine knocking is said to be pinging, with the final g dropped as in the clue
a pebble is a small stone
E is the baseball scorer's abbreviation for an error

explanation.surface: A rattling car engine turns out to have a pebble lodged in it by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in knockin' tells you the knocking word also drops its final g. E for error comes from baseball scorekeeping.
explanation.definitionFit: A piston engine is the standard internal-combustion motor that powers most cars.

clue.text: Forced to remove labels, getting up after I lob explosive

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters before it are rearranged
in a down entry, getting up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: letters reordered
to de-tag is to take off tags

explanation.surface: Someone is compelled to peel off labels after lobbing a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forced to' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at Forced.
explanation.definitionFit: Obligated means bound or compelled to do something, a past participle like forced.

clue.text: What comes after I behead a big cat: the beginning of your peril

indicators.note: beheading cuts off the top, so the animal's first letter goes
the beginning of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the next letter of the alphabet
a leopard is a big cat
the first letter of your

explanation.surface: Beheading a lion or tiger is the start of real danger for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What comes after I' sounds like a sequel, but it is the alphabet: J follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeopardy is danger or risk of harm, a noun synonym of peril.

clue.text: Something most women have: no egrets (oops, typo)

indicators.note: a typo jumbles letters by mistake, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A misprint turns the motto 'no regrets' into one about wading birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends the phrase is a typo for 'no regrets'; it is the anagram signal. ESTROGEN is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrogen is the main female sex hormone, present in nearly every woman's body.

clue.text: Onset of financial bubbles involves rent strike at first for people who have claimed, improbably, that their ideas are gaining support around the globe

definitions.text: people who have claimed, improbably, that their ideas are gaining support around the globe

indicators.note: the onset of something is its beginning, so only the opening letter is kept
to involve something is to take it in, so the rip word goes inside the foam word
at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the first letter of financial
lather is soapy foam made of bubbles
a rent is a rip in cloth
the first letter of strike

explanation.surface: A bubble economy begins with tenants refusing to pay rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke in the definition: people who think the world is flat say their movement is growing worldwide, which is a global claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat-earthers insist the planet is a disc, so a following that spreads 'around the globe' is an ironic boast.

clue.text: Punk helps to accommodate debut of chanteuse in drag

indicators.note: punk suggests something rough and disorderly, so the next word's letters are messed up
to accommodate is to give room to, so a letter is housed inside
a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter only

blocks.note: letters to be reordered
the first letter of chanteuse

explanation.surface: A punk rocker helps a nightclub singer launch her career as a drag act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In drag' suggests cross-dressing, but drag here is a verb meaning to haul.
explanation.definitionFit: To schlep, from Yiddish, is to lug or haul something heavy, the same as to drag.

clue.text: Performer and doctor grabbing walking cane

indicators.note: walking sets the word in motion, so its letters move about
grabbing something holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the usual abbreviation
letters reordered

explanation.surface: An actor and a physician fight over a walking stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walking cane' reads as a single object, but walking is the signal to mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer entertains an audience on stage, so is one kind of performer.

clue.text: Germanic language has metallic sound

indicators.note: the phrase has the answer inside it, carried across the word boundary

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: German, Dutch or a cousin is said to sound harsh and metallic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the stereotype that German sounds harsh; the answer straddles the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A clang is the loud ringing noise of metal striking metal.

clue.text: Death is yonder, with impressionist

blocks.note: yonder means over there
an aper is a mimic who imitates others

explanation.surface: A painter of the impressionist school ponders that death waits over there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impressionist' suggests Monet or Degas, but here it is someone doing impressions.
explanation.definitionFit: The grim reaper is the traditional personification of death, a figure with a scythe.

clue.text: Omit something from barrel I'd emptied

indicators.note: something taken from a phrase is a piece lying inside its letters

blocks.note: runs across the three words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A cask is drained, so its contents get left out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Emptied' looks like the instruction to drop middle letters, but it only lends its first letter to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to leave out a sound or a passage, a verb synonym of skip or omit.

clue.text: Place ointment around middle of scar

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, enclosing it
the middle of a word is its central letters only

blocks.note: a lotion is a soothing cream
the two central letters of scar

explanation.surface: Instructions to rub cream around a scar.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a site or spot, a plain synonym for a place.

clue.text: Retiring child outwardly into drilling apparatus

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the whole string is written backwards
outwardly keeps only the outside letters of the following word

blocks.note: a girl is a female child
the first and last letters of into

explanation.surface: A shy child is drawn to a drilling machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outwardly' looks attached to child but works on 'into'; GIRL plus IO then reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil rig is the platform and machinery used to bore wells for petroleum.

clue.text: Heaven is seen in exhibit

indicators.note: something seen in another is located inside it

blocks.note: to parade is to display or show off
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heaven appears in an art exhibition.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is the blissful afterlife, the same as heaven.

clue.text: Burns vote against returning African

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the voting word is read the other way

blocks.note: Ken Burns, the American documentary filmmaker
a nay is a vote of no

explanation.surface: A politician named Burns votes against a returning African.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burns' looks like a verb or the Scottish poet, but it is the American documentary maker.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kenyan is a person from Kenya in East Africa, an example of an African.
